extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders (workers, employers, trade associations, small businesses, and the general public) preparing public comments for OSHA rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and submitting effective public comments in OSHA rulemaking dockets, including what content to include, procedural timing, submission methods, and how to track your input. Applies to workers and other stakeholders who wish to influence OSHA regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly communicate whether you are for or against the proposed action
rubrics_metrics.description: "Clearly communicate whether you are for or against the proposed action, why, and how it impacts you"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your position up front and explain the reasons. Explain how the proposal would affect you, your coworkers, your workplace, or your industry in concrete terms so the agency can assess the practical impact of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide worker-centered evidence and personal workplace stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Include personal stories about workplace impacts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA emphasizes worker input because employees often know the most about hazards and fixes. Use first-hand accounts to illustrate hazards, compliance problems, or benefits. Where possible, tie anecdotes to frequency, severity, and real-world examples; cite specific tasks, equipment, locations, or incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer specific details and feasible suggestions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't only state opinions; propose concrete alternatives, specific regulatory language, compliance approaches, or implementation steps. Include technical details, data, standards, or references that support your recommendations and explain feasibility (costs, practicability). The guidance notes that feasibility concerns (e.g., from trade associations) have led to regulatory revisions in the past.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus comments on relevant sections of the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Address only relevant sections (you needn't comment on everything)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target your comments to the parts of the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) that affect you or where you have expertise. You do not need to comment on unrelated provisions; specific, focused comments are more useful to reviewers than broad, unfocused submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the rulemaking stages and time your participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven-stage rulemaking: Pre-Rule (RFI/ANPRM), Proposed Rule (NPRM; small business meetings; advisory committees), Final Rule Development (agency analyzes comments), Publication/Outreach (final rule, compliance dates, educational materials)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know where a rule is in the process to choose the best engagement method (e.g., respond to RFIs/ANPRMs to shape problem definition; comment on NPRMs to influence proposed requirements; participate in small business meetings or advisory committees during the proposed stage). Understanding stages helps you submit timely, relevant input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the prescribed submission channels and meet the deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Online at Regulations.gov, by mail, or in person; 11:59 PM ET deadline on stated due date
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified submission method in the Federal Register notice. Ensure your comment is submitted before the stated deadline (11:59 PM ET on the due date). If mailing or submitting in person, allow for processing time. Check the Federal Register notice for any docket-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and confirm your comment through official platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Track via Regulations.gov, RegInfo.gov, Federal Register, OSHA QuickTakes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, monitor the docket on Regulations.gov and related sites to confirm receipt, view agency postings, and follow rulemaking developments. Use tracking tools to receive updates on the rule's status and any subsequent outreach or compliance dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in stakeholder meetings and advisory committee opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in small business meetings and advisory committees during the proposed rule stage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA holds small business meetings and convenes advisory committees as part of the proposed rule stage; these are opportunities to present evidence, feasibility concerns, or technical recommendations directly. Use these venues when available to supplement written comments and to raise issues that may not be well-expressed in a docket filing.
